title: Fan-out on write, and where it breaks

spec.title: Fan-out on write, and where it breaks
spec.description: Precompute every follower's feed at post time so reads are a single cache lookup. Excellent until someone with ten million followers posts.

nodes.label: The celebrity problem
nodes.sublabel:
10M followers = 10M writes
for one post. Hybrid: fan out
normal users, pull for
celebrities at read time.

steps.text: The post is written once to the authoritative store. That part is cheap and bounded.
Fan-out is enqueued rather than done inline — the author's request returns immediately instead of waiting for millions of writes.
Workers insert the post ID into every follower's feed list. This is where the cost lives: one post becomes N writes, and N is the follower count.
A follower's feed is already assembled. Reading it is one cache lookup with no joins, no ranking across sources, and no fan-in — which is why this design wins for a read-heavy product.
An account with ten million followers posts. That single action becomes ten million cache writes, saturating the workers and delaying fan-out for everyone else on the queue.

The standard fix is hybrid: fan out on write for ordinary accounts, and for the small set of very-high-follower accounts skip fan-out entirely — merge their recent posts in at read time. Most users pay nothing; the expensive case is handled by the path that scales with it.
